questions.question: Dr. Afif, a dental surgeon, practices as a professional civil society (SCP). According to Article 1 of Law 9-88, is his structure subject to the accounting obligation?
options: No, SCPs are exempt from accounting
Yes, because any legal entity with merchant status is subject to it
Only if its turnover exceeds 5 million DH
No, only public limited companies are subject to this obligation
questions.explanation: Art. 1: any natural or legal person with merchant status must keep accounts. An SCP carrying on a for-profit activity falls within this scope.

questions.question: Dr. Touzani, practicing as a sole proprietor, generates a turnover of 2.3 million DH. Can he benefit from the simplifications provided for in Article 1?
options: Yes, because the threshold is 3 million DH for liberal professions
No, because his turnover exceeds the 2 million DH threshold
Yes, provided he keeps a detailed general ledger
No, dentists are excluded from the benefit of the simplifications
questions.explanation: Art. 1, para. 5: the 2,000,000 DH threshold applies to natural persons. Above that, simplifications are no longer accessible.

questions.question: Dr. Afif, whose turnover is 1.2 million DH, may he record his expenses on the basis of internal supporting documents?
options: No, all expenses must be supported by supplier invoices
Yes, provided they are signed by himself
No, only equipment purchases can be supported by internal documents
Yes, but only for expenses under 500 DH
questions.explanation: Art. 1, last bullet: small traders may record petty expenses on the basis of internal supporting documents signed by the trader.

questions.question: According to Article 2, what types of accounts must the dental practice's chart of accounts include?
options: Only balance sheet accounts
Statement of position accounts, management accounts, and special accounts
Only customer and supplier accounts
Only cash and fixed asset accounts
questions.explanation: Art. 2, para. 3: the chart of accounts must include statement of position account classes, management account classes, and special account classes.

questions.question: Is Dr. Touzani, whose turnover is 1.5 million DH, exempt from the general ledger according to Article 2?
options: Yes, because all companies are exempt from it
Yes, if the summary trial balance can be established directly from the journal
No, the general ledger is mandatory for medical professions
No, only companies can benefit from this exemption
questions.explanation: Art. 2, last para.: natural persons referred to in Article 1, para. 5 are exempt from the general ledger if the trial balance can be established directly from the journal.

questions.question: Dr. Afif uses subsidiary journals for his purchase and sales transactions. According to Article 3, how often must he centralize these entries?
options: Once a week for purchase transactions
Once a month, in accordance with the law
Once a quarter with court clerk authorization
Once a year at the close of the financial year
questions.explanation: Art. 3, para. 2: entries recorded in subsidiary journals are centralized once a month in the journal and general ledger.

questions.question: Can Dr. Touzani (turnover ≤ 2M DH) centralize his subsidiary journals at a different frequency than that provided for in Article 3?
options: No, monthly centralization is mandatory for everyone
Yes, he may centralize once per financial year at closing
Yes, provided he obtains approval from the administration
No, liberal professions have stricter specific rules
questions.explanation: Art. 3, last para.: small traders are authorized to centralize entries once per financial year at its close.

questions.question: Dr. Afif's practice, constituted as a company, generates a turnover of 8 million DH. What obligation does Article 4 impose on him?
options: The appointment of a statutory auditor
None, the 10 million DH threshold has not been reached
The establishment of an accounting organization manual
The annual publication of accounts in a newspaper
questions.explanation: Art. 4: the obligation of an accounting organization manual only applies to enterprises whose turnover exceeds 10,000,000 DH.

questions.question: According to Article 5, when must Dr. Touzani carry out the inventory of his assets and liabilities?
options: At the end of each semester
At least once per financial year, at its end
Only upon the transfer of his practice
Only at the request of the tax authorities
questions.explanation: Art. 5: inventory must be carried out at least once per financial year, at its end.

questions.question: Dr. Afif purchases a CBCT scanner for his practice. According to Article 14, at what value should he record it?
options: At its estimated replacement value
At its acquisition cost, including incidental expenses
At its resale value on the second-hand market
At the supplier's tax-exclusive list price
questions.explanation: Art. 14, para. 1: assets acquired for consideration are recorded at their acquisition cost (purchase price + incidental expenses).

questions.question: Dr. Touzani wishes to value his dental consumables inventory. According to Article 14, what methods may he use?
options: Only the selling price method
The weighted average cost or FIFO method
The LIFO method only
The last known purchase price method
questions.explanation: Art. 14, para. 9: fungible assets are valued either at their weighted average acquisition cost, or according to the FIFO principle.

questions.question: Can Dr. Afif (turnover ≤ 2M DH) benefit from a simplified method for valuing his inventory?
options: Yes, by estimating the purchase cost or based on the selling price with a reduction
No, simplified valuation is not authorized by law
Yes, but only for prosthetic inventory
No, only companies may use simplified methods
questions.explanation: Art. 14, last para., 1st bullet: small traders may carry out a simplified inventory valuation by estimating the purchase cost or based on the selling price with a reduction.

questions.question: Dr. Touzani carries out a revaluation of his fixed assets. According to Article 14, how should he treat the revaluation surplus?
options: He may use it to offset the year's losses
He must record it separately as a liability in the balance sheet
He must record it as extraordinary income
He must submit it to the approval of the Order of Dental Surgeons
questions.explanation: Art. 14, para. 8: the revaluation surplus cannot be used to offset losses; it is recorded separately as a liability in the balance sheet.

questions.question: According to Article 9, when must a dental practice constituted as a company prepare its financial statements?
options: At the request of the tax authorities
At the close of each financial year, based on accounting records and inventory
Every two years for liberal professions
Only when the articles of association are amended
questions.explanation: Art. 9: financial statements are prepared at the close of the financial year on the basis of accounting records and inventory.

questions.question: Dr. Afif finds that the application of accounting rules does not give a true and fair view of his situation. What does Article 19 provide?
options: He may depart from the rules by justifying it in the supplementary information statement
He must follow the rules without any possible exception
He must refer the matter to the court of first instance
He may change his presentation without justification
questions.explanation: Art. 19: in specific situations, it may be possible to depart from the requirements if they do not give a true and fair view, provided that the departure is mentioned and justified in the supplementary information statement.

questions.question: Dr. Touzani wishes to change the closing date of his financial year. What does Article 19 require of him?
options: Prior authorization from the court clerk
Simple notification to his chartered accountant
Justification in the supplementary information statement
Approval from the National Order of Dental Surgeons
questions.explanation: Art. 19, last para.: any change in the closing date must be duly justified in the supplementary information statement.

questions.question: Dr. Afif's practice (turnover 9 million DH) is exempt from which financial statements according to Article 21?
options: The balance sheet and income statement
The management balance sheet, financing statement, and supplementary information statement
Only the financing statement
Only the supplementary information statement
questions.explanation: Art. 21: enterprises whose turnover is less than or equal to 10,000,000 DH are exempt from the management balance sheet, financing statement, and supplementary information statement.

questions.question: Can Dr. Touzani (turnover 1.8 million DH) use the simplified balance sheet and income statement model according to Article 21?
options: No, the simplified model is not provided for by law
Yes, because his turnover is less than 10 million DH
Yes, but only for the balance sheet, not the income statement
No, because dentists are excluded from the benefit of the simplified model
questions.explanation: Art. 21, para. 2: persons referred to in the preceding paragraph are authorized to adopt the accounting framework according to the simplified model annexed to the law.

questions.question: Must Dr. Afif keep his supporting documents in national currency according to Article 22?
options: No, he may keep them in euros
Yes, all accounting documents are prepared in national currency
Yes, but only for invoices over 1,000 DH
No, the law does not specify the currency of documents
questions.explanation: Art. 22, para. 1: accounting documents are prepared in national currency.

questions.question: According to Article 22, for how long must Dr. Touzani keep his dental equipment purchase invoices?
options: 5 years
10 years
15 years
Until cessation of activity
questions.explanation: Art. 22, para. 2: accounting documents and supporting documents must be kept for ten years.

questions.question: If the tax authorities consider that Dr. Afif's accounting is not regular, what may they do according to Article 23?
options: They may reject the accounting and proceed with an adjustment
They must accept it if taxes have been paid
They may order a suspension of activity
They must refer the matter to the National Order of Dental Surgeons
questions.explanation: Art. 23: the tax authorities may reject accounting records that are not kept in the forms prescribed by law.

questions.question: Dr. Touzani entrusts his accounting to a chartered accountant. According to Article 24, what does the law require of him?
options: He must comply with a specific set of rules for dentists
He is required to comply with the provisions of Law 9-88
He must obtain special approval from the Ministry of Health
He may apply international IFRS standards
questions.explanation: Art. 24: chartered accountants and approved accountants are required to comply with the provisions of Law 9-88 for the accounting of the enterprises they handle.

questions.question: According to Article 10, what does the management balance sheet that a dental practice must prepare describe?
options: The formation of the net result and self-financing
The cash available at year-end
The number of patients treated per month
The amount of prosthetic fees invoiced
questions.explanation: Art. 10, para. 3: the management balance sheet describes the formation of the net result and self-financing.

questions.question: Dr. Afif (SCP, turnover 12 million DH) must prepare an accounting organization manual. According to Article 4, what is the purpose of this manual?
options: To describe the company's accounting organization
To list the practice's approved suppliers
To detail the medical procedures performed
To present the practice's fee schedule
questions.explanation: Art. 4: the manual is intended to describe the company's accounting organization.

questions.question: Dr. Touzani finds that several of his patients have not paid their fees. According to Article 16, how should he treat these doubtful receivables?
options: He must keep them at their nominal value without provision
He must take account of risks and make provisions if necessary
He may cancel them outright
He must declare them to the Order of Dental Surgeons
questions.explanation: Art. 16: account must be taken of risks and charges arising during the financial year. Doubtful receivables must be subject to impairment provisions.
